name: Where Fear and Weapons Meet
label: Revelation
lede: Two Morning Again alumni and a Poison the Well bassist cut fifteen songs in about twenty-one minutes for Revelation, then spent the next five years changing singers.

eras.title: Faster, simpler, no metal
eras.text: When Morning Again broke up, guitarist John Wylie and drummer Jason Lederman wanted something quicker and more fun than the metal-leaning hardcore taking over Florida. One five-song 7" got them onto Revelation.

years.h: Wylie and Lederman start over after Morning Again
years.p: Guitarist [[John Wylie|f587d49e-5157-4c8a-869c-c3f0f7b5b31c]] (ex-Culture, [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]]) and drummer Jason Lederman add [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]]'s Ryan Primack on bass and singer Alex "Wall Street Justice" Flores. They call themselves Where Fear and Weapons Meet.
years.xp: Per a fan-blog history of the band, Lederman came from Beyond Reason and [[Until the End|b366ca2e-a474-48b8-866c-e4d10fb1c1dc]]; Wylie had also played in Tension.

years.h: Five songs at Studio 13 become a 7" on Revelation
years.p: Recorded in Deerfield Beach and released as Revelation REV 74, which the label sold as traditional, fun, catchy hardcore. The first press had 220 copies on clear vinyl.
years.xp:
The back cover has a misprint: the fourth song is listed as Other Face, the same as the opener, instead of Above Water. The labels and lyric sheet get it right. And Never and Meant to Be are listed as two tracks but play as one song.

Jeff Caudill of [[Gameface|c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27]] did the layout.

eras.title: The Weapon, then a new voice
eras.text: The full-length is the record people still mean when they bring the band up. Singer Alex Flores and bassist Ryan Primack left the next year, and the band carried on through smaller labels with a different lineup.

years.h: The Weapon packs fifteen songs into about 21 minutes
years.p: Revelation REV 86, recorded in April 1999 at Studio 13 in Deerfield Beach. Chad from [[Shai Hulud|2aaa7913-72ae-469b-9fdb-4c79cd70ed2e]] and Steve from [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] sing backing vocals.
years.xp:
The credits use stage names: Alex Wall Street Justice on vocals, John Pain on guitar, Ryan Powers on bass, Jason Deucifer on drums. The gang vocals double as a roll call of the late-'90s South Florida scene.

Revelation's first press included 222 copies on orange vinyl.

years.h: Flores and Primack quit; Larry Scott takes the mic
years.p: The year after The Weapon, Flores and Primack leave. Larry Scott, co-owner of Think Fast! Records, sings, and Chad Kishick plays bass.
years.xp:
A fan blog calls The Weapon "considered to many their best work" and says the new lineup "lost a bit of its tightness and speed."

The same blog adds that Lederman was the only original member left for the 2000 to 2001 sessions, with players from the Miami bands Powerhouse and Backlash filling in.

years.h: A split with Comin' Correct lands on Temperance
years.p: The 2000 split with Comin' Correct comes out on Temperance Records.
The EP is the first release after Revelation, on Triple Crown Records, and the last before Flores comes back.

eras.title: Flores comes back
eras.text: A second guitarist from Until the End arrived, Flores returned to the mic for the last record on Eulogy, and in 2004 the band stopped.

years.h: Chip Walbert brings a second guitar from Until the End
Flores returns for Control, the last record
years.p: The EP comes out on Eulogy Recordings with Think Fast!, and it is the final release the band puts out.
years.xp: The fan blog says the band reunited its original lineup for Control, with Flores back on vocals.

yt: Final show, The Alley, Miami, April 2004
years.h: The band stops after one more year
years.p: Wylie, Flores and the rest walk away in 2004. Members' other bands include Against All Authority, Poison the Well, Shai Hulud, Morning Again and Until the End.

eras.title: One weekend in Pompano Beach
eras.text: A Florida reunion festival brought the band back for a weekend, with a mix of old members and later ones.

yt: Full set, Bringing It Back Fest 2, 2012
years.h: Back in Pompano Beach for Bringin' It Back for the Kids Fest 2
years.p: Wylie, Scott, Walbert and Kishick play the festival on October 12 and 13, alongside Trapped Under Ice, the Mongoloids and Backtrack.
years.xp: The reunion was announced in June. Punknews listed the lineup as original members plus Scott on vocals, Walbert and Kishick, with talk of more shows to come.
